LESSON: COUNTING CONCRETE OBJECTS

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.3: Counting concrete objects

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Counting concrete objects. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate one to one • Learners match numerals with correspondence while concrete objects for numbers 1-9 counting concrete objects • In groups or pairs, individually
2. enjoy counting concrete learners count people or objects in objects within their their class up to 9. environment • Learners to count concrete objects
3. appreciate the use of one to from 1-20 using ICT devices. one correspondence in real • Learners to play video games on life situations. counting

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: COUNTING CONCRETE OBJECTS
Counting concrete objects is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Counting concrete objects problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Counting concrete objects question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Counting concrete objects question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Counting concrete objects set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Counting concrete objects.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Counting concrete objects in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

2. enjoy counting concrete learners count people or objects in objects within their their class up to 9. environment • Learners to count concrete objects
